gate_reasoning: Stage 2 scores 36.6% High, 16.9% Medium, and 45.1% Low across 71 scored claims. The High-tier cluster is strong: all key utilization-inequality statistics (PMC6661624), non-adherence data (PMC11052292), Lancet diabetes control figures (PMC12681878), the Frontiers Jakarta CDM barriers study, and the Singapore Healthier SG RDD study are well-sourced peer-reviewed academic work. However, 45% of claims are Low primarily because (a) 12 claims carry ASSUMED-N tags with no primary source, (b) market sizing figures (supplement market, corporate wellness market, Aon medical inflation, Vinmec financials) rely on aggregator or trade-press sources only, (c) three claims have no source at all (IDR 46.4 trillion diabetes spend, complication cost $2,000–4,000/year, travel friction costs), and (d) the private hospital bed-supply fragmentation figure relies solely on a non-listed consultancy (L.E.K.). The five weak claims flagged for deep research are actionable — three require specific government or primary-filing source fetches (BPJS annual report, PERSI/Kemkes hospital database, Aon direct report). The ASSUMED-N claims are inherently field-interview dependencies and cannot be resolved by web research alone. The core epidemiological and policy narrative is well-evidenced. Ship with flag: mark the three unsourced claims as data gaps in the final report and queue the five deep-research actions before final stage compilation.
